title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Chop calms after a gnarly week, but the AI Kahuna wipes out
conditions.summary: Futures are modestly higher after last week's tech-led selloff, led by the Dow and small caps. Nvidia's slide and a big CPI report Tuesday keep the mood cautious.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: As of about 4:10 AM CT, S&P 500 futures were up about 0.4%, Nasdaq-100 futures up about 0.2% and Dow futures up about 0.7%; early quotes, and sources varied.
Russell 2000 futures were up roughly 1%, with small caps leading the bounce.
The 10-year Treasury yield was near 4.86%, slightly higher.
WTI crude fell about 1.2% to near $89.70; gold rose about 0.8% to near $4,108.
Bitcoin fell about 1.8% to near $74,500; the VIX eased about 5% to about 24.3.
No fresh dollar index reading was found in this morning's sources.
Asia: Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi rose more than 1% as chip stocks rebounded; Hong Kong gained modestly.
Europe: London's FTSE 100 was up about 0.8% in early trade.
Context: last week the Nasdaq Composite fell about 3.4% and the S&P 500 about 2.7%, led by tech.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: 9:00 AM CT: September wholesale inventories; no consensus found.
10:00 AM CT: New York Fed consumer inflation expectations for October; prior 1-year reading 3.9%.
Treasury sells 3- and 6-month bills at 10:30 AM CT and 3-year notes at 12:00 PM CT.
One calendar lists Fed speakers today including Chicago Fed President Goolsbee around 9:00 AM CT and Richmond Fed President Barkin around 11:15 AM CT.
Main story: the Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% in October with two votes for a hike, and futures reportedly price high odds of a December hike.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Berkshire Hathaway: Q3 operating earnings of about $12.7 billion, down about 6% on weaker insurance results; cash hit a record $377.4 billion. Shares slightly higher pre-market.
Before the open today: Constellation Energy (EPS estimate about $3.90) and KKR.
After the close today: Occidental Petroleum (EPS estimate about $1.43), Take-Two Interactive and Rocket Lab.
Also on today's calendar: The Trade Desk, Hims & Hers, Lucid, Archer Aviation and Plug Power.
About 82% of S&P 500 companies that have reported so far beat estimates, per LSEG data.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: NVDA (Nvidia): about -4.5% — the company opened an internal investigation tied to reports about CEO Jensen Huang; details are unconfirmed.
KKR (KKR & Co.): about +3.7% — rising ahead of its results this morning.
CRWV (CoreWeave): about -3% — slipping ahead of its earnings Tuesday after the close.
AMAT (Applied Materials): about +1.7% — chip equipment name firm ahead of Thursday's report.
INTC, MRVL, QCOM (Intel, Marvell, Qualcomm): down about 0.5% to 1.2% — chip stocks under pressure alongside Nvidia.
MSFT, GOOGL, META (Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta): up less than 1% — big tech steadier after last week's drop.
SKHY (SK Hynix US listing): about -3.5% overnight — even as its Seoul shares closed slightly higher.

sections.title: Business News
items: Binance named Justin Yek as CFO, replacing Kaiser Ng in what it called a planned move, as it reimburses customers after a large crypto theft last month.
Democrats are reportedly drafting proposals on data center power costs, independent AI testing and AI liability; nothing has been enacted.
TSMC shares rose about 4.7% in Taipei as Asian chip stocks rebounded; its October sales are due Tuesday.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index posted its worst week since March 2025 last week.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 8:30 AM CT open: whether Nvidia's pre-market slide deepens or stabilizes, and how chip stocks follow.
10:00 AM CT: New York Fed inflation expectations, ahead of Tuesday's CPI.
After the close: Occidental Petroleum and Take-Two Interactive earnings.

sections.title: Earnings This Week
items: Mon: Constellation Energy (CEG), before open — data center power demand.
Mon: KKR (KKR), before open — fundraising and deal activity.
Mon: Occidental Petroleum (OXY), after close — production volumes and oil prices.
Mon: Take-Two Interactive (TTWO), after close — game release outlook.
Mon: Rocket Lab (RKLB), after close — launch cadence and backlog.
Tue: Sea Limited (SE), before open — e-commerce and gaming growth.
Tue: CoreWeave (CRWV), after close — contract backlog and data center spending plans.
Thu: Nebius (NBIS), before open — AI cloud capacity growth.
Thu: Cisco (CSCO), after close — networking orders tied to AI infrastructure.
Thu: Applied Materials (AMAT), after close — chip equipment demand from AI and memory.

sections.title: Economic Calendar This Week
items: Mon 9:00 AM CT: Wholesale inventories (Sept).
Mon 10:00 AM CT: NY Fed consumer inflation expectations (Oct) — prior 1-year 3.9%.
Tue 7:30 AM CT: CPI (Oct) — consensus +0.3% m/m headline, +0.2% m/m core.
Tue: Fed Governor Waller speaks on the economic outlook.
Wed: Veterans Day — bond market closed, stock market open.
Thu 7:30 AM CT: Weekly jobless claims.
Thu: Fed Governor Barr speaks on AI and inequality.
Fri 7:30 AM CT: PPI (Oct) — consensus +0.4% m/m.
Fri: Fed Vice Chair Jefferson speaks on productivity and new technology.
Backdrop: the next Fed meeting is Dec 8-9, with markets weighing the odds of a rate hike.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Monday, November ninth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Riding shotgun on the beach towel this morning is my co-anchor, Gus the wonder dog, fresh from chasing seagulls. Give the crew a howdy, Gus! Alright, let's check the swell. After a gnarly week that knocked the Nasdaq down more than three percent, the water is calming a bit on the Dawn Patrol. As of about four A M Central, S and P 500 futures were up about four tenths of a percent. Nasdaq 100 futures were up about two tenths. Dow futures were up about seven tenths, and Russell 2000 small cap futures were up roughly one percent. The ten year yield sits near four point eight six percent. Crude is down about one percent, gold is up nearly one percent, bitcoin slipped about two percent, and the VIX eased to around twenty four. Overseas, Asian chip stocks bounced, and London was higher. Wind and weather now. Today's calendar is light. Wholesale inventories come out at nine A M Central, and the New York Fed's consumer inflation expectations survey lands at ten A M Central. The big story is the Fed itself. Rates are being held, but traders are now betting on a possible hike in December. Tide chart. Berkshire Hathaway reported over the weekend. Operating earnings fell about six percent, mostly from weaker insurance results, but its cash pile hit a record of about three hundred seventy seven billion dollars. This morning, Constellation Energy and K K R report before the bell. After the close, watch Occidental Petroleum, Take-Two Interactive and Rocket Lab. Now the lineup. The Kahuna of A I chips, Nvidia, is wiping out, down about four and a half percent pre-market. The company opened an internal investigation tied to reports about C E O Jensen Huang, and the details are still unconfirmed. Other chip names like Intel, Marvell and Qualcomm are slightly lower. Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta are up less than one percent. And K K R is up nearly four percent ahead of its earnings this morning. That's a wave worth catching. Treat time, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Beach talk. Binance named a new chief financial officer in a planned handoff. In Washington, Democrats are preparing proposals on data center power costs and A I safety testing, though nothing has passed. Sets to watch today. Nvidia at the open, the inflation expectations survey at ten A M Central, and the evening earnings from Occidental and Take-Two. Now, it's Monday, so here's the week's swell forecast. Tuesday is the big one. The October consumer price index lands at seven thirty A M Central. Forecasters expect headline prices up three tenths of a percent and core up two tenths. Sea Limited reports before the open, and CoreWeave reports after the close. Wednesday is Veterans Day. The bond market is closed, but stocks are open. Thursday, weekly jobless claims come out at seven thirty A M Central. Nebius reports before the open. After the close, Cisco and Applied Materials report, a double check on A I spending. Friday, the producer price index arrives at seven thirty A M Central, with a forecast gain of four tenths of a percent. The two sets most likely to make waves are Tuesday's inflation report and Thursday night's Cisco and Applied Materials numbers. Soul surfers, stay patient, and skip the hodads.
